question: The international agreement Montreal Protocol is related to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ozone layer.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The international agreement Montreal Protocol is related to the ozone layer.​
 
• It is related to the Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer.
 
• It is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer from **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**.
 
• It was** signed in 1987 **and **came into force in 1989.**
 
• 16 September is celebrated as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Ramsar Convention on Wetlands:**

 
 
• The Convention on Wetlands of International Importance is the first modern* treaty between nations aimed at conserving natural resources. *
 
• The signing of the Convention on Wetlands was done in **1971 at Ramsar, Iran.**
 
• There are a total of **75 Ramsar sites** in India.(as of Feb 2022)
 
• **Chilika Lake **was the** first Ramsar site in India.​**
 
 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] In News__**

__
 
• As of July 2022:

 
 
• Five new wetlands of International importance have been designated in India.
 
• With this, the total number of Ramsar sites in the country has increased from 49 to 75 Ramsar sites.
 
• Union Minister of Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav said, “Delighted to inform that 5 more Indian wetlands have got Ramsar recognition as wetlands of international importance.”
 
• The five newly designated wetlands are:
 
 
• Karikili Bird Sanctuary, Tamil Nadu
 
• Pallikaranai Marsh Reserve Forest, Tamil Nadu
 
• Pichavaram Mangrove, Tamil Nadu
 
• Pala wetland, Mizoram
 
• Sakhya Sagar, Madhya Pradesh.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage sites:**

 
 
• These sites are of cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of importance.
 
• The **Galapagos Islands and Quito **were the first world heritage sites in the world.
 
• **Ajanta Caves, Ellora Caves, Agra Fort, and Taj Mahal** were the **first World Heritage sites in India.**
 
• There is a total of **40 world heritage sites in India.​**
 
 

 
• India now has 75 Ramsar sites after the addition of 11 new sites in August 2022.
